```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Neant_2023_covid19_news2"))$reference`
* Article: [CPT Pharmacometrics Syst Pharmacol 2023;12(12):2027](https://doi.org/10.1002/psp4.13051)
  (open access, PMC10725266). The subgroup and standard-of-care fits are in the
  Supporting Information (Appendix S1, Tables S1-S3).

Neant et al. fitted nasopharyngeal SARS-CoV-2 viral load and the National Early
Warning Score 2 (NEWS-2) simultaneously in hospitalised COVID-19 patients of the
DisCoVeRy trial (standard of care with or without remdesivir). Viral load
follows a target-cell limited model with an eclipse phase and separate
infectious / noninfectious virion pools; the normalised viral load drives an
effect compartment, and NEWS-2 is a Hill function of the log10 effect-compartment
viral load. Remdesivir reduces viral production by a fraction `eps`.

The paper reports four fits of this structure, each a separate model here:

| Model | Fit | Source |
|-------|-----|--------|
| `Neant_2023_covid19_news2` | all 664 patients, both arms (final model) | Table 2 |
| `Neant_2023_covid19_news2_highvl` | patients with admission viral load >= 3.5 log10 copies/10^4 cells | Table S1 |
| `Neant_2023_covid19_news2_lowvl` | patients with admission viral load < 3.5 log10 copies/10^4 cells | Table S2 |
| `Neant_2023_covid19_news2_soc` | standard-of-care arm only, no remdesivir effect | Table S3 |

Table S4 (NEWS-2-only refits used to show that the viral-load link improves the
fit by 169 BIC units) is a robustness check that conditions on individual
empirical Bayes estimates and is not packaged.

# Population

The analysis set is 664 hospitalised adults from 48 sites in France, Belgium,
Portugal, Austria and Luxembourg, randomised between March 2020 and January
2021 to standard of care (SoC, N = 329) or SoC plus intravenous remdesivir
(200 mg on Day 1 then 100 mg once daily for up to 10 days, N = 335). Patients
were randomised at most 20 days after symptom onset (median 9 days, IQR 7-11);
456 (68.7%) were male and 349 (52.5%) were younger than 65 years; NEWS-2 was
>= 7 at randomisation in 74.5% (SoC) and 67.7% (remdesivir). Viral load was
missing at randomisation for 39.8% (SoC) and 34.0% (remdesivir) of patients
(Table 1). Data were collected before variants of concern and before
vaccination.

The same information is available programmatically via
`rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Neant_2023_covid19_news2"))$population`.

# Source trace

The per-parameter origin is recorded as an in-file comment next to each `ini()`
entry in `inst/modeldb/therapeuticArea/Neant_2023_covid19_news2*.R`. The values
of the four fits are collected below; random-effect SDs are on the log scale
(logit scale for N0 and eps).

| Parameter | Main (Table 2) | High VL (Table S1) | Low VL (Table S2) | SoC (Table S3) |
|-----------|----------------|--------------------|-------------------|----------------|
| `R0` (SD) | 6.71 (0.50, held) | 7.31 (0.50) | 7.60 (0.50) | 6.17 (0.50) |
| `delta` < 65 / >= 65 y (1/day) (SD) | 0.84 / 0.74 (0.30) | 0.75 / 0.70 (0.17) | 0.63 / 0.62 (0.18) | 0.89 / 0.80 (0.32) |
| `p` (virions/cell/day) (SD) | 1.56e5 (1.56) | 3.06e6 (0.14) | 2.55e3 (1.35) | 1.42e5 (1.70) |
| `ke0` < 65 / >= 65 y (1/day) (SD) | 0.82 / 0.37 (1.42) | 0.52 / 0.33 (1.34) | 1.1 / 0.29 (1.65) | 1 / 0.29 (1.61) |
| `n` Hill (SD) | 1 (0.23) | 1.44 (0.34) | 0.94 (1.15) | 0.98 (0.28) |
| `LVL50` (log10 copies/10^4 cells) (SD) | 4.81 (0.72) | 6.07 (0.52) | 3.33 (0.77) | 4.43 (0.72) |
| `N0` (logit SD) | 0.86 (3.35) | 1.5 (1.63) | 1.15 (3.78) | 0.8 (3.33) |
| `eps` (logit SD) | 22% (2.43) | 78% (1.81) | 15% (0.8) | n/a |
| Additive error, log10 viral load | 1.23 | 1.19 | 1.02 | 1.34 |
| Additive / proportional error, NEWS-2 | 1.53 / 0.04 | 1.47 / 0.05 | 1.59 / 0.03 | 1.56 / 0.04 |

| Equation / constant | Value | Source location |
|---------------------|-------|-----------------|
| `d/dt(target)`, `d/dt(eclipse)`, `d/dt(infected)`, `d/dt(virus)`, `d/dt(virus_ni)` | n/a | Equation 1; production terms with `(1 - eps)` from Equation 4 |
| `beta = R0 * c * delta / (p * T0 * mu)` | n/a | Methods, definition of R0 |
| `d/dt(effect) = ke0 * Vobs - ke0 * effect` | k1e = ke0 | Equation 2 and the k1e = ke0 assumption |
| `news2 = N0 + (20 - N0) * log10(E)^n / (log10(E)^n + LVL50^n)` | maximum 20 | Equation 3 |
| `k`, `c`, `mu` | 4 /day, 10 /day, 1e-4 | Methods, 'Assumptions on parameter values' |
| `T0`, initial conditions | 4e6 cells; I1 = 0, I2 = 1, Vi = Vni = 0 | Methods, 'Assumptions on parameter values' |
| `f` (`fscale`) | 2.5e-6 | Methods: 10^-3 x 10^4 / (4 x 10^6) |
| Incubation period `tinc` | median 5 days, SD 0.125 | Methods (prior on the time of infection) |
| `N0` bounds | 0 to 3, logit-normal | Methods and Table 2 footnote |

# Typical trajectories

Model time is days since infection. Observation rows carry `dvid = 1` and no
`cmt`: both endpoints (`log10_viral_load`, `news2`) are algebraic and are
returned on every row.

```{r typical}
mod <- readModelDb("Neant_2023_covid19_news2")

obs_grid <- function(times, ...) {
  tibble::tibble(time = times, evid = 0L, dvid = 1L, cmt = NA_integer_, ...)
}

ev_typ <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  obs_grid(seq(0, 45, by = 0.1), id = 1L, AGE_GE65 = 0L, TRT_REMDESIVIR = 0L),
  obs_grid(seq(0, 45, by = 0.1), id = 2L, AGE_GE65 = 1L, TRT_REMDESIVIR = 0L)
)
typ <- rxode2::rxSolve(rxode2::zeroRe(mod), events = ev_typ,
                       returnType = "data.frame") |>
  dplyr::mutate(age = ifelse(id == 1, "< 65 years", ">= 65 years"))

typ_summary <- typ |>
  dplyr::group_by(age) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    peak_vl = max(log10_viral_load),
    tsymptom_peak_vl = tsymptom[which.max(log10_viral_load)],
    peak_news2 = max(news2),
    tsymptom_peak_news2 = tsymptom[which.max(news2)],
    tsymptom_news2_below_3 = min(tsymptom[tsymptom > tsymptom_peak_news2 & news2 < 3]),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
knitr::kable(typ_summary, digits = 2)

stopifnot(
  # Fig. 1 shows peak loads of roughly 4-7 log10 copies/10^4 cells near symptom
  # onset. An exponent slip in p, T0 or f moves the peak by orders of magnitude.
  all(typ_summary$peak_vl > 3.5 & typ_summary$peak_vl < 6),
  all(abs(typ_summary$tsymptom_peak_vl) < 5),
  # The slower ke0 of patients aged >= 65 years delays the NEWS-2 recovery.
  diff(typ_summary$tsymptom_news2_below_3) > 2
)
```

```{r typical-plot, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 3.5}
typ |>
  dplyr::select(tsymptom, age, `log10 viral load` = log10_viral_load,
                `NEWS-2` = news2) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(c(`log10 viral load`, `NEWS-2`)) |>
  dplyr::filter(tsymptom >= -3, tsymptom <= 40) |>
  ggplot(aes(tsymptom, value, colour = age)) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~name, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(x = "Time since symptom onset (days)", y = NULL, colour = "Age",
       caption = paste("Typical-value trajectories (no random effects, no",
                       "treatment); compare the shapes of Figure 1."))
```

## Effect compartment on the normalised viral-load scale

Equation 2 writes the effect-compartment input as `Vi + Vni`, while Equation 3
compares `log10(E)` with `LVL50` expressed in log10 copies/10^4 cells. The
packaged models drive the effect compartment with the normalised viral load
`f * (Vi + Vni)`, so that `E` and `LVL50` share a scale. The maintainers checked
both readings against the paper's own simulation results: with the normalised
input the model reproduces the reconstructed share of high-viral-load patients
at randomisation (37.8%) and the time-to-improvement medians and treatment
gains of Figure 2 (next section), whereas feeding the unscaled virion count adds
about 5.6 log10 units to `log10(E)` and roughly doubles every median time to
clinical improvement (about 24 days instead of 11.4 in low-viral-load,
high-risk patients). Once `E` falls below 1 copy/10^4 cells the Hill input is
held at 0, so the score returns to the baseline N0 instead of taking the log of
a vanishing number.

# Replicate Figure 2: antiviral efficacy and time to clinical improvement

The paper simulated 5000 patients with the population's sex and age
proportions, started a hypothetical antiviral of fixed efficacy (0%, 80%, 90%,
99% or 99.9% inhibition of viral production) at randomisation, and computed the
time from randomisation to NEWS-2 < 3 (patients with NEWS-2 < 7 at
randomisation) or < 5 (NEWS-2 >= 7), stratified by viral load (< or >= 3.5
log10 copies/10^4 cells) and NEWS-2 (< or >= 7) at randomisation.

Here 200 virtual patients are reused across the five efficacy scenarios, so
each scenario is compared with the untreated course of the same patients. The
random effects are drawn in base R and passed as parameters to the
zero-random-effect model, which makes the cohort identical on every machine.
The paper sampled the time from infection to randomisation from a fitted Gamma
distribution whose parameters are not reported; it is approximated here as the
individual incubation period plus a Gamma(shape 10, scale 0.93) time from
symptom onset to randomisation (median 9 days, IQR about 7-11, as in Table 1),
truncated at the 20-day inclusion limit. 47.5% of patients are aged >= 65
years (Table 1).

```{r fig2-cohort}
set.seed(20231205)
n_pat <- 200L
omega <- rxode2::rxode(mod)$omega
eta <- matrix(rnorm(n_pat * nrow(omega)), n_pat) %*% chol(omega)
colnames(eta) <- rownames(omega)

age_ge65 <- rbinom(n_pat, 1, 0.475)
tinc <- 5 * exp(eta[, "etaltinc"])
onset_to_rand <- qgamma(runif(n_pat, 0, pgamma(20, shape = 10, scale = 0.93)),
                        shape = 10, scale = 0.93)
trand <- round((tinc + onset_to_rand) * 10) / 10

efficacy <- c(0, 0.8, 0.9, 0.99, 0.999)
fig2_grid <- seq(0, 65, by = 0.1)

ev_fig2 <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(seq_along(efficacy), function(k) {
  tidyr::expand_grid(pat = seq_len(n_pat), time = fig2_grid) |>
    dplyr::mutate(
      id = (k - 1L) * n_pat + pat,
      efficacy = efficacy[k],
      trand = trand[pat],
      AGE_GE65 = age_ge65[pat],
      TRT_REMDESIVIR = as.integer(efficacy[k] > 0 & time >= trand[pat] - 1e-8),
      evid = 0L, dvid = 1L, cmt = NA_integer_
    )
})) |>
  dplyr::arrange(id, time)

# A fixed efficacy replaces the estimated remdesivir eps: the typical logit is
# set to the scenario's efficacy and its random effect to zero. The 0% scenario
# never switches the treatment indicator on, so its eps value is unused.
params_fig2 <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(seq_along(efficacy), function(k) {
  data.frame(id = (k - 1L) * n_pat + seq_len(n_pat), eta,
             check.names = FALSE) |>
    dplyr::mutate(logiteps = qlogis(max(efficacy[k], 0.5)), etalogiteps = 0)
}))

sim_fig2 <- rxode2::rxSolve(
  rxode2::zeroRe(mod), events = ev_fig2, params = params_fig2,
  keep = c("efficacy", "trand"), covsInterpolation = "locf",
  returnType = "data.frame"
)
```

```{r fig2-outcomes}
# Time from randomisation to clinical improvement, censored at 35 days (the
# x-axis limit of Figure 2).
outcome <- sim_fig2 |>
  dplyr::group_by(id) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    efficacy = efficacy[1],
    at_rand = which.min(abs(time - trand[1])),
    vl_rand = log10_viral_load[at_rand],
    news2_rand = news2[at_rand],
    threshold = ifelse(news2_rand < 7, 3, 5),
    t_improve = {
      ok <- time >= trand[1] - 1e-8 & news2 < threshold[1]
      if (any(ok)) min(min(time[ok]) - trand[1], 35) else 35
    },
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    pat = (id - 1L) %% n_pat + 1L,
    vl_group = ifelse(vl_rand >= 3.5, "high viral load", "low viral load"),
    risk = ifelse(news2_rand >= 7, "NEWS-2 >= 7", "NEWS-2 < 7")
  )

untreated <- outcome |>
  dplyr::filter(efficacy == 0) |>
  dplyr::select(pat, t_untreated = t_improve, vl_group, risk)

strata <- untreated |>
  dplyr::count(vl_group, risk) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    simulated = 100 * n / sum(n),
    published = c(9.2, 28.6, 28.9, 42.5)[match(
      paste(vl_group, risk),
      c("high viral load NEWS-2 < 7", "high viral load NEWS-2 >= 7",
        "low viral load NEWS-2 < 7", "low viral load NEWS-2 >= 7"))]
  )
strata |>
  dplyr::rename(`Viral load at randomisation` = vl_group,
                `NEWS-2 at randomisation` = risk, `Patients` = n,
                `Simulated (%)` = simulated, `Paper, Results (%)` = published) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1)
```

```{r fig2-medians}
median_times <- untreated |>
  dplyr::group_by(vl_group, risk) |>
  dplyr::summarise(simulated = median(t_untreated), .groups = "drop") |>
  dplyr::mutate(published = c(14.6, 18.6, 5.8, 11.4)[match(
    paste(vl_group, risk),
    c("high viral load NEWS-2 < 7", "high viral load NEWS-2 >= 7",
      "low viral load NEWS-2 < 7", "low viral load NEWS-2 >= 7"))])
median_times |>
  dplyr::rename(`Viral load at randomisation` = vl_group,
                `NEWS-2 at randomisation` = risk,
                `Simulated median (days)` = simulated,
                `Paper, Results (days)` = published) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1)

gains <- outcome |>
  dplyr::filter(efficacy > 0) |>
  dplyr::select(pat, efficacy, t_improve) |>
  dplyr::left_join(untreated, by = "pat") |>
  dplyr::mutate(gain = t_untreated - t_improve)

gain_table <- gains |>
  dplyr::group_by(vl_group, risk, efficacy) |>
  dplyr::summarise(median_gain = median(gain), .groups = "drop") |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = efficacy, values_from = median_gain,
                     names_prefix = "eff_")
gain_table |>
  dplyr::rename(`Viral load at randomisation` = vl_group,
                `NEWS-2 at randomisation` = risk,
                `80%` = eff_0.8, `90%` = eff_0.9, `99%` = eff_0.99,
                `99.9%` = eff_0.999) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1, caption = paste(
    "Median gain in time to clinical improvement versus no treatment (days).",
    "Paper, high viral load: 1.3 / 1.4 days at 80% and 2.0 / 2.2 days at",
    "99.9% (NEWS-2 < 7 / >= 7); low viral load: less than 0.2 days in every",
    "scenario."))

pooled_gain <- gains |>
  dplyr::group_by(vl_group, efficacy) |>
  dplyr::summarise(median_gain = median(gain), .groups = "drop")
gain_hi_999 <- pooled_gain$median_gain[pooled_gain$vl_group == "high viral load" & pooled_gain$efficacy == 0.999]
gain_hi_80 <- pooled_gain$median_gain[pooled_gain$vl_group == "high viral load" & pooled_gain$efficacy == 0.8]
gain_lo_max <- max(pooled_gain$median_gain[pooled_gain$vl_group == "low viral load"])
median_by_vl <- untreated |>
  dplyr::group_by(vl_group) |>
  dplyr::summarise(m = median(t_untreated), .groups = "drop")

stopifnot(
  # Share of patients with a high viral load at randomisation (paper 37.8%).
  abs(mean(untreated$vl_group == "high viral load") * 100 - 37.8) < 12,
  # Share with NEWS-2 >= 7 at randomisation (paper 71.1%).
  abs(mean(untreated$risk == "NEWS-2 >= 7") * 100 - 71.1) < 15,
  # High viral load delays improvement by about 7 days (Results).
  diff(median_by_vl$m) < -3,
  # Antiviral gain: about 2 days at 99.9% and 1.3-1.4 days at 80% in high
  # viral load, essentially none in low viral load.
  gain_hi_999 > 1, gain_hi_999 < 5,
  gain_hi_80 > 0.5, gain_hi_80 < 3,
  gain_lo_max < 0.5
)
```

```{r fig2-plot, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 6}
fig2 <- outcome |>
  dplyr::select(pat, efficacy, t_improve) |>
  dplyr::left_join(untreated |> dplyr::select(pat, vl_group, risk), by = "pat") |>
  dplyr::group_by(vl_group, risk, efficacy) |>
  dplyr::arrange(t_improve, .by_group = TRUE) |>
  dplyr::mutate(cum_incidence = 100 * dplyr::row_number() / dplyr::n()) |>
  dplyr::ungroup() |>
  dplyr::filter(t_improve < 35)

ggplot(fig2, aes(t_improve, cum_incidence,
                 colour = factor(100 * efficacy))) +
  geom_step() +
  facet_grid(risk ~ vl_group) +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0, 35), ylim = c(0, 100)) +
  labs(x = "Time since randomisation (days)",
       y = "Cumulative incidence of clinical improvement (%)",
       colour = "Antiviral efficacy (%)",
       caption = paste("Replicates Figure 2 of Neant 2023 (200 virtual",
                       "patients reused across scenarios)."))
```

The simulated strata proportions match the published reconstruction, the
median times to improvement are within about 4 days of the published values,
and the antiviral gains show the published pattern -- a benefit of one to two
days confined to patients with a high viral load. In a 1500-patient run of the
same design the maintainers obtained gains of 1.4 / 1.7 days at 80% and 2.3 /
3.6 days at 99.9% efficacy in high-viral-load patients (NEWS-2 < 7 / >= 7),
against 1.3 / 1.4 and 2.0 / 2.2 days in the paper, and 0.2 days or less in
low-viral-load patients, as published. The infection-to-randomisation
distribution, which sets how far past the viral peak each patient is when
stratified, is approximated, and the high-viral-load, NEWS-2 < 7 stratum holds
only a handful of the 200 virtual patients.

## Random effect on ke0 and the tail of Figure 2

The published curves reach about 95% improvement or more by Day 35 in every
panel, whereas the simulated curves level off lower in high-risk patients.
The difference comes from the random effect on `ke0`, whose SD of 1.42 (log
scale, Table 2) gives a sizeable share of virtual patients an effect
compartment that empties over months. Re-solving the untreated scenario with
that random effect removed (keeping the strata of the full solve) brings the
share not improved by Day 35 down to the few percent of Figure 2. In a
1500-patient run re-stratified on the solve without the `ke0` random effect,
the maintainers obtained medians of 13.3, 19.3, 5.0 and 10.8 days against the
published 14.6, 18.6, 5.8 and 11.4 days. The paper does not state which random
effects entered its simulation, so the packaged model keeps the Table 2 value;
the comparison is shown only to locate the discrepancy.

```{r fig2-ke0}
params_no_ke0 <- params_fig2 |>
  dplyr::filter(id <= n_pat) |>
  dplyr::mutate(etalke0 = 0)
sim_no_ke0 <- rxode2::rxSolve(
  rxode2::zeroRe(mod), events = dplyr::filter(ev_fig2, efficacy == 0),
  params = params_no_ke0, keep = c("efficacy", "trand"),
  covsInterpolation = "locf", returnType = "data.frame"
)
no_ke0 <- sim_no_ke0 |>
  dplyr::group_by(id) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    at_rand = which.min(abs(time - trand[1])),
    threshold = ifelse(news2[at_rand] < 7, 3, 5),
    t_no_ke0 = {
      ok <- time >= trand[1] - 1e-8 & news2 < threshold[1]
      if (any(ok)) min(min(time[ok]) - trand[1], 35) else 35
    },
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  dplyr::select(pat = id, t_no_ke0)

ke0_check <- untreated |>
  dplyr::left_join(no_ke0, by = "pat") |>
  dplyr::group_by(vl_group, risk) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    median_with = median(t_untreated),
    median_without = median(t_no_ke0),
    pct_not_improved_with = 100 * mean(t_untreated >= 35),
    pct_not_improved_without = 100 * mean(t_no_ke0 >= 35),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  dplyr::left_join(dplyr::select(median_times, vl_group, risk, published),
                   by = c("vl_group", "risk"))
ke0_check |>
  dplyr::rename(`Viral load at randomisation` = vl_group,
                `NEWS-2 at randomisation` = risk,
                `Median, ke0 random effect (days)` = median_with,
                `Median, no ke0 random effect (days)` = median_without,
                `Paper median (days)` = published,
                `Not improved by Day 35, ke0 random effect (%)` = pct_not_improved_with,
                `Not improved by Day 35, no ke0 random effect (%)` = pct_not_improved_without) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1)

stopifnot(
  # The ke0 random effect is what holds a fifth or more of the cohort above
  # the improvement threshold at Day 35.
  mean(untreated$t_untreated >= 35) - mean(no_ke0$t_no_ke0 >= 35) > 0.08
)
```

# Remdesivir in the trial setting

With the estimated remdesivir efficacy (22%, logit-normal SD 2.43) given for 10
days from randomisation, the model predicts only a small difference between the
arms, in line with the paper's conclusion that remdesivir's antiviral effect was
too small to change NEWS-2 meaningfully.

```{r trial}
ev_trial <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(1:2, function(arm) {
  tidyr::expand_grid(pat = seq_len(n_pat), time = fig2_grid) |>
    dplyr::mutate(
      id = (arm - 1L) * n_pat + pat,
      trand = trand[pat],
      AGE_GE65 = age_ge65[pat],
      TRT_REMDESIVIR = as.integer(arm == 2L & time >= trand[pat] - 1e-8 &
                                    time < trand[pat] + 10 - 1e-8),
      arm = c("SoC", "SoC + remdesivir")[arm],
      evid = 0L, dvid = 1L, cmt = NA_integer_
    )
})) |>
  dplyr::arrange(id, time)
# The same patients in both arms, each with their own drawn remdesivir
# efficacy (the etalogiteps column of the eta draws).
params_trial <- data.frame(id = seq_len(2 * n_pat),
                           rbind(eta, eta), check.names = FALSE)

sim_trial <- rxode2::rxSolve(
  rxode2::zeroRe(mod), events = ev_trial, params = params_trial,
  keep = c("arm", "trand"), covsInterpolation = "locf",
  returnType = "data.frame"
)

trial <- sim_trial |>
  dplyr::group_by(id) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    arm = arm[1],
    at_rand = which.min(abs(time - trand[1])),
    threshold = ifelse(news2[at_rand] < 7, 3, 5),
    vl_day5 = log10_viral_load[which.min(abs(time - trand[1] - 5))],
    t_improve = {
      ok <- time >= trand[1] - 1e-8 & news2 < threshold[1]
      if (any(ok)) min(min(time[ok]) - trand[1], 35) else 35
    },
    .groups = "drop"
  )
trial_summary <- trial |>
  dplyr::group_by(arm) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    `Mean log10 viral load, Day 5 after randomisation` = mean(vl_day5),
    `Mean time to clinical improvement (days)` = mean(t_improve),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
knitr::kable(trial_summary, digits = 2)

# Same patients in both arms: the per-patient difference isolates the drug.
trial_gain <- trial |>
  dplyr::mutate(pat = (id - 1L) %% n_pat + 1L) |>
  dplyr::select(pat, arm, t_improve, vl_day5) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = arm, values_from = c(t_improve, vl_day5)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    gain = `t_improve_SoC` - `t_improve_SoC + remdesivir`,
    vl_drop = `vl_day5_SoC` - `vl_day5_SoC + remdesivir`
  )
trial_gain |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    `Median gain in time to improvement (days)` = median(gain),
    `Mean gain in time to improvement (days)` = mean(gain),
    `Mean viral load reduction at Day 5 (log10)` = mean(vl_drop)
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2)

stopifnot(
  # Remdesivir lowers viral load on average, but moves the time to clinical
  # improvement by well under the ~2 days of a near-complete antiviral.
  mean(trial_gain$vl_drop) > 0.05,
  abs(median(trial_gain$gain)) < 1,
  abs(mean(trial_gain$gain)) < 1
)
```

# Subgroup and standard-of-care fits (Tables S1-S3)

```{r subgroups, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 3.5}
fits <- c(
  "Main (Table 2)" = "Neant_2023_covid19_news2",
  "High VL (Table S1)" = "Neant_2023_covid19_news2_highvl",
  "Low VL (Table S2)" = "Neant_2023_covid19_news2_lowvl",
  "SoC (Table S3)" = "Neant_2023_covid19_news2_soc"
)
sub_typ <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(names(fits), function(nm) {
  m <- readModelDb(fits[[nm]])
  ev <- obs_grid(seq(0, 45, by = 0.1), id = 1L, AGE_GE65 = 0L,
                 TRT_REMDESIVIR = 0L)
  if (nm == "SoC (Table S3)") ev$TRT_REMDESIVIR <- NULL
  rxode2::rxSolve(rxode2::zeroRe(m), events = ev, returnType = "data.frame") |>
    dplyr::mutate(fit = nm)
}))

sub_summary <- sub_typ |>
  dplyr::group_by(fit) |>
  dplyr::summarise(peak_vl = max(log10_viral_load), peak_news2 = max(news2),
                   .groups = "drop")
knitr::kable(sub_summary, digits = 2,
             caption = "Typical patient aged < 65 years, no treatment.")

peak <- setNames(sub_summary$peak_vl, sub_summary$fit)
stopifnot(
  # The subgroups were split on admission viral load, so the typical peak of
  # the high-viral-load fit lies above, and of the low-viral-load fit below,
  # the main fit (p differs by about 1.3 log10 units each way).
  peak[["High VL (Table S1)"]] > peak[["Main (Table 2)"]] + 0.5,
  peak[["Low VL (Table S2)"]] < peak[["Main (Table 2)"]] - 0.5,
  abs(peak[["SoC (Table S3)"]] - peak[["Main (Table 2)"]]) < 0.5
)

sub_typ |>
  dplyr::select(tsymptom, fit, `log10 viral load` = log10_viral_load,
                `NEWS-2` = news2) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(c(`log10 viral load`, `NEWS-2`)) |>
  dplyr::filter(tsymptom >= -3, tsymptom <= 40) |>
  ggplot(aes(tsymptom, value, colour = fit)) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~name, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(x = "Time since symptom onset (days)", y = NULL, colour = NULL)
```

# NCA

The models contain no drug pharmacokinetics -- remdesivir enters only as an
on-treatment indicator with a constant fractional effect -- so there is no
concentration profile for PKNCA to summarise, and the paper reports no NCA
metrics. Validation relies on the published strata, median times and treatment
gains reproduced above.

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Effect-compartment scale.** Equation 2 is encoded with the normalised viral
  load `f * (Vi + Vni)` as input rather than the virion count, so that
  `log10(E)` is on the scale of `LVL50` (log10 copies/10^4 cells); see the
  section on the effect compartment above for the evidence.
* **Floor on log10(E).** `log10(E)` is held at 0 when `E` < 1 copy/10^4 cells.
  The paper does not say how the Hill term was evaluated once the viral load
  fell below one copy, where the logarithm turns negative and a non-integer
  Hill exponent is undefined.
* **NEWS-2 residual error.** The paper reports additive and proportional
  components without the combination rule; the Monolix `combined1` form
  (SD = a + b * f) is used.
* **Viral load floor.** `log10_viral_load` adds 1e-10 to the normalised load so
  the logarithm is finite at the infection time. Values below the limit of
  detection (1 log10 copies/10^4 cells) were censored in the original fit.
* **Time axis.** Model time is days since infection, with one productively
  infected cell at time 0. The paper estimated each patient's infection time
  with a log-normal incubation-period prior (median 5 days, SD 0.125); this is
  carried as `tinc` with a non-estimated random effect, and the output
  `tsymptom = time - tinc` gives days since symptom onset. Event tables must
  place randomisation and treatment on the days-since-infection axis.
* **Remdesivir indicator.** `TRT_REMDESIVIR` is time-varying: 1 only while
  remdesivir is given. The paper does not state when the effect stopped in the
  fit; the trial simulation above uses the 10-day maximum course, and the
  Figure 2 scenarios keep the antiviral on through follow-up because the paper
  only says it started at admission.
* **Infection-to-randomisation distribution.** The fitted Gamma distribution
  used by the paper is not reported; it is approximated from the incubation
  prior and the Table 1 symptom-onset-to-randomisation median and IQR.
* **Figure 2 tail.** With the Table 2 SD of 1.42 on the `ke0` random effect,
  about a fifth to a quarter of simulated patients have not improved by Day
  35, against about 5% in the published Figure 2; omitting that random effect
  reproduces the published curves closely (see the section above). The
  packaged value follows Table 2.
* **Cohort size.** Figure 2 used 5000 simulated patients; this vignette reuses
  200 across scenarios, so the smallest stratum holds only a handful of
  patients.
* **Table S2 ke0 for patients aged < 65 years.** The value cell in the
  supplement reads '(29.60)' with the estimate carried by a Word multilevel
  list number rather than typed text. That list level is formatted '%1.%2'
  starting at 1, so it displays as 1.1; the model uses 1.1 /day.
* **Subgroup sizes.** The number of patients in the high- and low-viral-load
  fits (Tables S1 and S2) is not reported; Table 1 lists 183 and 236 patients
  with an observed admission viral load in the two bands.
* **Table S4** (NEWS-2-only refits) is a robustness check that conditions on
  individual empirical Bayes estimates and is not packaged.
